Senator Baldaoci, Representative Roberts, and members of the Joint Standing Committee on Inland Fisheries and Wildlife, my name is Amanda Egan, Executive Director of Maine Woodland Owners, speaking today in support of LD 2221.
Maine Woodland Owners is a statewide nonprofit that advances stewardship of Maine's small woodland resources through the encouragement of sustainable forest management, support for the state's 86,000 small private woodland owners, and a land trust that conserves working forests.
Our organization sen/es on this board and values the opportunity it creates for constructive dialogue and relationship development between stakeholders. As recreational pressure on private lands increases, this board serves as a vitalvenue
to bring together those who care about public access and to encourage the
resolution of complex challenges.
We support the expansion of the board to include representatives from ATV clubs,
the nonmotorized recreation industry, and the North Maine Woods. Giving these
groups a formal seat at the table ensures that they are part of the solution-making process and allows for the direct resolution of friction points before they lead to
landownerfrustration or land closures. When more voices are present, the resulting

LD 2221 matches the board to the reality of outdoor recreation in Maine's woods

Testimony in Support of L.D. 2221
An Act to Amend the Composition of the Landowners and Land Users Relations Advisory Board
Sponsored by Senator Baldacci of Penobscot March 2, 2026
Good afternoon, Senator Baldacci, Representative Roberts, and distinguished members of the Inland Fisheries and Wildlife Committee.
My name is Jeff McCabe, and I serve as Director of the Maine Office of Outdoor Recreation. I am pleased to provide testimony in support of L.D. 2221, An Act to Amend the Composition of the Landowners and Land Users Relations Advisory Board.
The proposed updates to the Board's composition are an important and thoughtful reflection of the stakeholders who should be engaged in the critical conversations between landowners and land users. As outdoor recreation continues to evolve, it is essential that the Board's membership reflects the full diversity of recreation interests across our state.
Maine's outdoor recreation economy depends on maintaining continued opportunities for traditional uses -- including hunting, fishing, motorized recreation, nonmotorized recreation, and boating -- while also recognizing and planning for new and emerging outdoor activities. Ensuring representation from trending outdoor recreation sectors will strengthen dialogue, foster collaboration, and support balanced decision-making.
We strongly support the inclusion of three representatives of outdoor recreationists, including one representative of an all-terrain vehicle club and one representative of a nonmotorized recreation industry with a focus on hiking, wildlife watching, biking, paddling, trail running, or other popular outdoor pursuits. This broader representation ensures that the Board reflects the evolving ways in which people responsibly access and enjoy Maine's lands.
We also support the continued inclusion of non-voting seats for relevant state agencies. These positions are vital not only for sharing information and data, but also for ensuring that agencies hear stakeholder perspectives firsthand. Effective collaboration depends on clear communication and shared understanding.
Additionally, we believe that one seat for the Department of Economic and Community Development is appropriate, and we appreciate the ongoing efforts and leadership of the Departments of Inland Fisheries and Wildlife and Agriculture, Conservation and Forestry in supporting responsible land access across Maine.

TESTIMONY BEFORE THE JOINT STANDING COMMITTEE ON INLAND FISHERIES AND WILDLIFE
IN SUPPORT OF LD 2221
An Act to Amend the Composition of the Landowners and Land Users Relations Advisory Board
March 2, 2026
Senator Baldacci, Representative Roberts, and members of the Joint Standing Committee on
Inland Fisheries and Wildlife, my name is Jo D. Saffeir, and I am the Deputy Commissioner of the Maine Department of Agriculture, Conservation and Forestry (DACF). I am testifying in support of LD 2221, An Act to Amend the Composition of the Landowners and Land Users
Relations Advisory Board.
This bill is an outcome of the work completed last month by the Public Access to Private Land
Working Group. That Group, which DACF and the Department of Inland Fisheries and Wildlife
co-chaired, was charged with recommending actions and policies to incentivize private landowners to maintain and expand recreational access to their lands and thereby ensure Maine's continued tradition of public recreational access to private land. As you heard in the report-out presented to this Committee a couple of weeks ago, the Working Group's consensus recommendations covered topics such as enforcement, education and outreach, legislation, landowner liability, land conservation, and more.
The Working Group also recommended this action before you today, to update the membership of the Landowners and Land Users Relations Advisory Board, to "be used as an ongoing forum to continue discussions, monitor emerging issues, and advance the recommendations outlined in [the] report." The Working Group recognized that this Advisory Board, with expanded membership, would have the expertise and commitment necessary to ensure the recommendations are implemented.
DACF strongly supports the proposed additions to the Advisory Board and looks forward to this
Board actively working to implement the Working Group's recommendations.
Thank you for your consideration. I would be happy to answer any questions now or at the work
session.

BEFORE THE JOINT STANDING COMMITTEE ON INLAND FISHERIES AND WILDLIFE

Reported by: Senator BALDACCI of Penobscot

Good afternoon, Senator Baldacci, Representative Roberts and members of the Inland Fisheries and Wildlife Committee. I am Kris MacCabe, Landowner Relations Corporal for the Maine Warden Service speaking on behalf of the Department of Inland Fisheries and Wildlife, in
support of L.D. 2221 An Act to Amend the Composition of the Landowners and Land Users
Relations Advisory Board.
This bill comes before you as a result of Resolve Chapter 82 (LD 1308), Directing the
Department of Inland Fisheries and Wildlife and the Department of Agriculture, Conservation
and Forestry to Examine Issues Related to Public Access to Privately Owned Lands. After extensive discussions with Working Group members in 2025, one of the key priorities identified
by the Working Group was to continue addressing these issues through the already established Landowners and Land Users Advisory Board and this bill will help that priority. This bill advances that recommendation by strengthening and refining the Board's composition to better reflect t0day's access landscape.
Specifically, the bill amends the membership of the Landowners and Land Users Relations Advisory Board by:
0 Increasing the number of outdoor recreationist representatives; 0 Adding greater specificity regarding the qualifications and experience required of those
members; 0 Adding a representative from an organization that manages recreational access to the
North Maine Woods; and 0 Adding five nonvoting members: two representatives from the Department's Bureau of
Warden Service, one representative from the Department of Economic and Community Development, and two representatives from the Department of Agriculture, Conservation
and Forestry.
These changes are directly aligned with the findings of the Working Group report, which states that the "legislative recommendations are intended to reduce landowner risk, Claflfll accountability, and support the long-term sustainability ofMaine 's access tradition. Ensuring the long-term stability ofMaine 's public access tradition requires statutory updates that reflect

modern recreational pressures and provide clearer protections for landowners. As new uses, technologies, and visitation patterns increase the potential for environmental damage, landowners have expressed growing concern about their exposure to cleanup and restoration costs. Strengthening Maine 's legal framework can help address these concerns, reinforce shared
responsibility among users, and encourage continued public access to private lands. "
Current statute already requires the Board to conduct an organizational review every five years to
assess whether additional or different representation is needed. Both the Board and the Department believe that these adjustments are appropriate at this time and will help carry forward the goals identified by the Working Group.
By broadening representation and ensuring relevant expertise is at the table, this bill will
strengthen collaboration between landowners, recreationists, and state agencies, and help secure the future of Maine's longstanding public access tradition.
For these reasons, the Board and the Department strongly support this bill.
